howTo.title: How do I submit a request?
howTo.intro: Three steps from signing in to receiving the official letter.
howTo.step1Title: Sign in with your university account
howTo.step1Body: Use your university email ending in @uoturath.edu.iq through the Google button.
howTo.step2Title: Fill in the request and upload the signed form
howTo.step2Body: Choose the request type, complete its details and upload the official form once it is signed by the responsible body.
howTo.step3Body: The request goes to the college dean, then Scientific Affairs, then the Vice President for Scientific Affairs, with a notification at every stage.

meaning.predatory_journal: The list's maintainers noted practices at this journal that are considered signs of predatory publishing, such as weak peer review or false indexing claims. A listing is a warning that calls for checking, and a journal's practices can change over time.
meaning.predatory_publisher: The list's maintainers noted practices at this publisher that are considered signs of predatory publishing. Its journals call for caution; check each journal on its own.
meaning.hijacked: A website uses the name of a real journal without being its official site. Papers sent to the fake site are not published in the real journal. Confirm the official site before you submit.

entry.whatToDo: Run the journal check, verify indexing on the official Scopus and Web of Science sites, and talk to Scientific Affairs if you will rely on the paper for promotion or another official procedure.
entry.disclaimer: This page shows what a volunteer-run, unofficial public list contains; it is not Al-Turath University's judgement of the journal or publisher. The lists of the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research and the decision of Scientific Affairs prevail.

checkPage.title: Journal Check: Is This Journal Reputable or Predatory?
checkPage.description: A free pre-submission journal check that matches a name, ISSN or website against predatory and hijacked journal lists and OpenAlex, Crossref and DOAJ.
checkPage.intro: Enter a journal name, ISSN or website. The check compares it with the predatory journal, predatory publisher and hijacked journal lists and with open sources, then shows the result and its reasons.
checkPage.how1: "Danger" means a match with a predatory or hijacked list or the department's list; do not submit before consulting Scientific Affairs.
checkPage.how2: "Caution" means signs that call for a manual check.
checkPage.how3: "Found in sources" only means the journal is known to the open sources; it is not a quality certificate.
checkPage.how4: The Scopus status always shows "unknown" because no Scopus API is available; check Scopus manually.
checkPage.advisory: The result is advisory. The Ministry's lists and the Scientific Affairs decision prevail.
